title: Snake Island: Why 4,000 Deadly Vipers Rule This Forest
description:
Thirty-three kilometers off the coast of São Paulo, Brazil, sits Ilha da Queimada Grande—better known as Snake Island—a steep 43-hectare Atlantic rainforest island so densely populated by venomous golden lancehead pit vipers (Bothrops insularis) that the Brazilian Navy prohibits unauthorized civilians from stepping ashore.

Online rumors claim five snakes wait on every square meter. Field surveys by São Paulo's Instituto Butantan show no evidence of that exaggerated myth, yet confirm an extraordinary real density: roughly 2,000 to 4,000 deadly vipers across the island, reaching up to 50 to 90 vipers per hectare in prime forest habitat.

Trapped roughly 11,000 years ago when rising seas flooded the land bridge to mainland Brazil without ground mammals, thousands of vipers climbed into the trees to ambush migratory birds at neck and eye height—evolving fast-acting venom up to five times more potent against avian prey.
